Has anyone tried this yet? It's definitely going to be in the next order I make, one way or another, but let's hear from the community on this one. An FA flavoring that recommends 20%? Insanity.

There are also reports of it being almost identical to the tobacco base used by Indigo Vapors. Which excites me a little more than it should; Indigo was one of my all-time favorite vendors back in the day I used to buy my juice pre-mixed. If it proves to be true, or at the very least just turns out to be a decent tasting tobacco vape, it will probably reside in my regular rotation of concoctions.

edited to add: dat shipping tho... holy smokes, sixteen smackers for two 10ml bottles of the stuff. I'm pulling the trigger, but it better be worth it.

This arrived in the mail today, a good week and a half and almost three days in customs later (not to mention the astronomical shipping fee, but that's expected when buying stuff like this overseas).

I've got a bunch of straight flavor ratios mixed up and I'm tooting along with clouds hanging low in the garage tonight, so I expect my next 'Let's Look At...' feature will probably be this. Give it a little time, I've got to try mixing this with stuff I just have a feeling it'll be delicious with so I can get a little better handle on it.

If you want a little bit of a sneak peek, my initial impressions if you will, here you go:

So I've read that it's similar to bases used by Indigo, and I've got to say that I do agree with what I've heard. It definitely tastes a little bit like the base to Duke, for instance. It's a nutty, woody, almost cedar-style taste to a smooth and earthy tobacco. Certainly on the sweeter end of the spectrum. If you want a good comparison, go to ecigexpress, check out Flavor Express (or Tobacco Express) flavors, get a bottle of FE Golden Virginia, and mix that up at around 6-7%. Vape it, and imagine you're tasting something a bit better than that. Like that, but better.

While on lunch or walking from one part of the building to another, how do you deal with your end users that have a quick question that isn't quick.
It depends, but generally i just delegate.

"Open a ticket" or "Send me an email." If they learn that they can come directly to the source with issues, they'll forever circumvent the established processes that are in place to deal with these issues.

It's the whole "If everything is urgent, nothing is" scenario. Every user thinks their situation is unique, and pressing.
Email the help-desk and it will be addressed as soon as possible.

Assuming they are rambling... "Sorry, I don't have much time, I'm [on lunch | going to x], send my team an email, and we'll look into it"

Or if they need personal help... It depends on the person whether I'll check with them later or not. ;)

"I would need my computer in front of me to look into that. Can you send in a ticket and I'll handle it asap." I say that with a positive attitude. When someone else handles the ticket and I get confronted I say "I let them handle it because they are [better | faster | available], and I knew how important it is to get you going."

I just slowly raise my hand and stick my fingers in their mouth while their talking and it usually takes care of it. :)

Seriously though, you can politely say "I'm afraid I might forget, can you please email the helpdesk".
